name: US inflation
summary: FRED index data imply US CPI inflation of about 4.1% in October, up from 4.0%, inside the 3.0–4.5% Watch band
state: FRED CPI index data imply annual US consumer price inflation of about 4.1% in October, up from 4.0% in September and rising for three consecutive months (FRED). That is inside the 3.0–4.5% Watch band and below the 4.5% Alert line. No newer figure was out on 24 Nov; November CPI is due in mid-December.
for_you: Higher US inflation tends to keep borrowing costs elevated and feeds through to prices of imported goods and services.
rubric_hit: CPI 4.1% y/y within 3.0–4.5% Watch band; rising 3 months

sources.title: FRED — CPI for All Urban Consumers (CPIAUCSL)

why: Inflation sets Fed policy and thus global borrowing costs; a resurgence would keep rates high for everyone.
drivers: Energy, tariffs, wages, housing costs, supply chains.

rubric.watch: CPI 3.0–4.5%, or rising for 3 consecutive months.
